item.text:
**6B.9 Research Note: Shehbaz Sharif (2024)**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning no. There is real evidence that the Sharif government tried to formalize some social-policy delivery through BISP, education, and minority/women/children bodies. But most of the durable-looking pieces were either executive-led, still incomplete, or offset by a strong record of media pressure, protest restrictions, weak accountability, and abusive treatment of vulnerable groups. That makes “durable institutions beyond personal rule” only partially supported.

**Supports durability**
- **IMF-backed multi-year reform program with BISP expansion** | **IMF** | **2024-07-12** | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) | The program was described as endorsed by federal and provincial governments and aimed to broaden the tax base, improve SOEs, strengthen competition, enhance human capital, and scale up BISP social protection. This is the strongest evidence for an institution-building agenda rather than ad hoc patronage. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.8`
- **BISP digitalization into Social Protection Wallets** | **APP** | **2024-03-18** | [URL](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/) | Sharif ordered BISP disbursements onto digital wallets to improve transparency and reduce discretion and leakage. That is a concrete step toward rule-based delivery that could outlast a single officeholder if maintained. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.7`, `6B.8`
- **BISP says aid is nonpartisan and transparent** | **Benazir Income Support Programme** | **2024-05-23** | [URL](https://www.bisp.gov.pk/NewsDetail/MjU0NDA1ZTItM2NiOC00NGE4LWJmNzctNGFiZTY4ZDFiZGFj) | BISP explicitly says assistance goes to poor and deserving people regardless of political affiliation and should be delivered through a transparent, dignified process. That supports an institutional rather than personal loyalty model. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`
- **Education emergency and Daanish Schools expansion** | **Dawn** | **2024-04-10** | [URL](https://www.dawn.com/news/1826827) | Sharif announced an education emergency and said the state would expand Daanish Schools into underserved areas for poor children. This points to a longer-horizon social-institution agenda, not just one-off relief. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.8`, `6B.6`
- **Minority-rights implementation discussions** | **Press Information Department, Pakistan** | **2024-04-30** | [URL](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/25171) | The law ministry said it was discussing implementation of minority-rights protections, the Christian Marriage Act, sanitation-worker safety, and a stronger National Commission for Minorities. This is modest but real institutional maintenance. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.8`, `6B.7`
- **Legislative measures for vulnerable groups** | **Press Information Department, Pakistan** | **2024-12-10** | [URL](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27376) | The government said it had enacted measures for women, children, human rights, and minorities, and strengthened related commissions. If accurate and implemented, this is the clearest pro-institution statement for durable social protection. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.8`, `6B.7`
- **Crisis-resilient social protection for poor and vulnerable households** | **World Bank** | **2024-06-20** | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/20/pakistan-world-bank-approves-535-million-for-crisis-resilient-social-protection-and-climate-smart-growth-in-the-livestoc) | The World Bank said Pakistan was strengthening social protection for poor and vulnerable households, including support for female farmers and food security. That suggests some institutional resilience to shocks, though it is still partly donor-backed. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.8`
- **Child welfare tied to education and safe conditions** | **Press Information Department, Pakistan** | **2024-11-19** | [URL](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27169) | Sharif linked child welfare to access to quality education, healthcare, and safe conditions, and pointed to Daanish Schools for underprivileged children in remote areas. This is the clearest public-facing welfare-institution statement in late 2024. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.8`, `6B.6`

**Counters durability**
- **Clampdown on media, NGOs, and opposition** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-01-11** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) | HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, NGOs, and opposition, creating self-censorship and weakening independent oversight. That is the opposite of building institutions that survive personal rule. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`
- **Weak social security and undocumented Afghan vulnerability** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-01-11** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) | HRW said the government failed to ensure adequate social security and left undocumented Afghans exposed to abuse and blocked access to employment and education. That undercuts any claim of durable inclusive institutions. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.8`
- **Forced evictions of low-income residents and street vendors** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-05-28** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor) | Authorities evicted poor residents and vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement. This suggests state capacity was still being used coercively, not institutionalized as durable social protection. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.6`
- **Ahmadi community harassment and blocked rites** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-06-21** | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocked religious rites for Ahmadis, with authorities failing to protect them. That is strong evidence against durable rights-protecting institutions. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.8`, `6B.7`, `6B.6`
- **Protest law criminalized peaceful assembly** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-09-09** | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) | Amnesty said the new law expanded state power to restrict gatherings rather than protect them. Institutional durability is weak if protest rights can be narrowed so quickly. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`
- **Crackdown on PTI protests** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-10-09** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against peaceful protesters. That is strong evidence that coercive security practice still dominated over durable civic institutions. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.6`
- **Judicial independence weakened by the 26th Amendment** | **The Guardian** | **2024-10-21** | [URL](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | Critics said the amendment weakened judicial independence and passed amid intimidation allegations. That directly cuts against building durable institutions that can outlast a ruler. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`
- **Digital/media control deepened by late 2024** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-12-12** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown) | HRW said internet throttling, VPN restrictions, and PECA-based controls were expanding while X remained blocked. A more controlled information environment is not a durable independent institution set. | `6B.9` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a new social institution that was clearly insulated from Sharif’s personal control and likely to survive a change in ruler.
- The best positive items are mostly executive-led reforms, not self-sustaining institutions with proven independence.
- So the most defensible reading is: Sharif strengthened some institutional mechanisms on paper and in delivery channels, but 2024 does not show a clearly durable, autonomy-protected social-institution legacy.
